messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to find public libraries with certain facilities:

1) In New York (NYC presumably), have Reading Room AND Fiction section.

2) In Los Angeles, have Wi-Fi AND Children Section.

3) In Chicago, have Cafe AND Reading Room.

We need to use the tool `public_library_find_nearby` which takes location and facilities list. We can call it three times? But we might combine multiple facilities per request; but each facility param expects one of enumerated values or array? It says facilities: "Wi‑Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That seems ambiguous: maybe it's an array of strings from those options. So we should pass all required ones as array.

Thus we will make calls:

First: location="New York, NY", facilities=["Reading Room","Fiction"]

Second: location="Los Angeles, CA", facilities=["Wi-Fi","Children Section"] note case: "Wi‑Fi". Use exactly "Wi-Fi".

Third: location="Chicago, IL", facilities=["Cafe","Reading Room"]

We'll produce JSON output after calling each function. We'll do them sequentially. Let's proceed.
